title: Marketplace & Partner Revenue: Reconciliation, Invoicing, and Forecast Treatment
author: Elena Park
body:
Overview

This playbook defines how Redwood Inference recognizes, invoices, forecasts and reconciles revenue that flows through marketplace partners, reseller arrangements, and partner-integrated billing flows. It covers accounting policy decisions, operational steps for month-end close, procurement/PO handling when partners act as resellers, contract requirements, and a set of reconciliations and controls that must run daily, weekly, and monthly.

Scope

- Applies to: marketplace integrations, partner-resold subscriptions, referral/commission arrangements, and partner-managed invoices where Redwood is the primary or agent.
- Excludes: direct self-serve hosted API customers billed via Redwood Console (see standard revrec playbook).
- Effective for agreements executed or materially modified on or after 2026-01-01.

Principles and Accounting Treatment Summary

1) Determine Role: For each partner contract, legal must classify Redwood as "principal" or "agent" for revenue recognition. Key indicators: price-setting ability, inventory risk (not usually applicable), primary responsibility for fulfillment, credit risk.
2) If Principal: Recognize gross revenue for the amount billed to end customers, and record partner commissions as operating expense (COGS/commission) based on contract.
3) If Agent: Recognize revenue net of partner fees (recognize only fee retained).
4) Timing: Revenue recognized over time for committed capacity subscriptions (ratable), or at point-in-time for one-off marketplace transactions (e.g., one-time connector install charge).
5) Deferred revenue: capture any billed-but-not-earned amounts in Deferred Revenue GL accounts and recognize per accepted schedule.

Contract & Legal Requirements (minimum clause checklist)

Every partner agreement supporting marketplace/reseller flows MUST include the following clauses before operational onboarding: 

- Role definition: explicit language clarifying whether Redwood is acting as principal or agent.
- Data-of-sale and customer identification: partner must provide signed customer details and PII-handling commitments.
- Pricing & billing responsibility: who sets list price, who collects payment, and chargeback/credit mechanics.
- Audit & reporting rights: Redwood audit access to partner transaction logs and settlement reports; frequency: monthly with 90 days lookback.
- SLA and indemnity: obligations for uptime, data incidents, and financial indemnity clauses.
- Commission schedule & clawback: explicit commission %, payment timing, and clawback triggers (refunds/cancellations within 60 days).
- KYC/AML and sanctions screening attestation (per compliance policy).

Procurement & PO Handling (when partners act as resellers)

1) Purchase order routing: All partner POs must be submitted to finance-inbound@redwood.com and reference the Redwood partner ID.
2) PO validation checklist (AP team): verify partner contract exists, PO amount matches contracted list price, customer details present, tax applicability confirmed.
3) Receipt & acceptance: document acceptance of customer onboarding (successful provisioning event) — this is the trigger for revenue to begin to ratably recognize for subscription deals.

Operational Billing Flows (patterns)

A. Partner collects payment (partner-merchant-of-record)
- Redwood invoices partner per settlement cadence (monthly) for usage or committed capacity.
- Redwood recognizes revenue based on whether Redwood is principal/agent: typically principal when Redwood delivers inference services directly.
- Settlement file format: CSV or Parquet with columns: settlement_id, partner_id, customer_id, transaction_date, invoice_amount, tax_amount, partner_fee, currency.

B. Redwood collects payment; partner references (partner-ref)
- Redwood bills end customer; partner gets commission via separate settlement invoice.
- Commission journals booked as expense; commission liabilities are tracked under Partner Payable.

Sample settlement CSV schema (text table)

| Column | Description | Required |
| settlement_id | Unique settlement identifier | Y |
| partner_id | Redwood partner GUID | Y |
| customer_id | Redwood customer GUID (if known) | Y |
| transaction_date | ISO-8601 date | Y |
| revenue_amount | Gross revenue charged to customer | Y |
| partner_fee | Fee or commission payable to partner | N |
| tax_amount | Collected sales tax | N |
| invoice_ref | Redwood invoice reference (if applicable) | N |

Reconciliation Rules and Controls

Daily (automated):
- Ingest partner settlement file and run match to Redwood billing ledger (billing_events table). Thresholds: 99.5% dollar match required; exceptions flagged to Partner Ops inbox.
- Basic schema validation: checksum, row counts, expected currency.

Weekly (finance ops):
- Aged exceptions report: mismatched rows >48 hours are escalated to Partner Ops and Contract Owner.
- Commission accrual sanity check: compute expected commission vs partner-submitted partner_fee; mismatch tolerance 0.5%.

Monthly (month-close):
- Gross-to-net reconciliation: verify gross billings, partner payouts, deferred revenue rollforward, and commission expense postings.
- Materiality thresholds: discrepancies > $5k or >0.5% of monthly partner revenue require formal variance memo and investigation.

Journal Entries & GL Mapping (examples)

- When Redwood is principal (monthly subscription billed by Redwood directly):
  - Dr Accounts Receivable (AR) — customer invoiced amount
  - Cr Revenue — recognized portion based on ratable schedule
  - Dr COGS/Partner Commission (when paid or accrued)
  - Cr Partner Payable
- When Redwood is agent (partner is merchant-of-record):
  - Dr Receivable from Partner (settlement amount net of partner fee)
  - Cr Revenue (net amount retained)
  - Dr Commission Expense — if there are referral fees/bonuses

Forecasting & Budget Treatment

- Revenue Forecasting: Partner-sourced bookings are tracked in a separate forecast line item ("Partner Marketplace"). Use weighted pipeline approach (Probability * ARR) and a separate conversion lag profile: settlements typically lag 1 billing cycle for partners that collect funds, so recognized revenue is modeled with a 1–2 cycle timing adjustment.
- Budgeting: commission expense and settlement timing must be modeled as a separate expense category. Treat partner integration professional services as capitalizable or OPEX per policy (consult FP&A).
- Sensitivity scenarios: include a baseline, -15% partner conversion, and +30% acceleration scenarios for quarterly planning.

Month-End Close Runbook (Partner Revenue)

1) Day -5 to 0: Ingest final settlement files; ensure all partner POs and provisioning receipts are recorded.
2) Day 0: Run gross-to-net reconciliation job and produce dashboard snapshot (Finance Console -> Partner Revenue -> Monthly Close).
3) Day 1: Post journal entries for deferred revenue rollforward and commission accruals.
4) Day 3: Close AR for the partner segment and validate GL balances against subledger.
4) Day 5: Publish partner revenue pack to leadership with variance commentary and any open exceptions.

Roles & Ownership

- Partner Ops: operational ingestion, partner relationship, first-line reconciliation; owns partner onboarding checklist.
- Finance (Revenue Accounting): final classification of principal/agent, revrec policy, journal entries, month-close ownership.
- Legal: contract clauses, audit rights, dispute resolution ownership.
- FP&A: forecasting, scenario modeling, budget consolidation.
- SRE/Platform: provide provisioning and event logs for proof of service (used by Finance to support recognition).

Dispute & Refund Handling (operational steps)

1) All refunds/credits reported by partner or customer must be recorded in the partner settlement file and flagged in the monthly reconciliation.
2) Short-term impact (<60 days): adjust commission clawback via debit memo to partner payable.
3) Material disputes (>= $10k or >0.5% monthly partner revenue): trigger joint review with Legal and generate a remediation plan within 10 business days.

Automation & Tooling Recommendations

- Mandatory: partner settlement ingestion job (SFTP/S3) with schema validation and automated matching to billing_events.
- Recommended: small dashboard in Redwood Console showing partner daily revenue trends, exception counts, and open disputes.
- Long-term: embed partner contract metadata (principal/agent flag, commission rate, settlement cadence) in the billing platform so GL mapping is automated at invoice generation.

Appendix B — Quick Checklist for Partner Onboarding (Finance/Legal)

- Legal: signed partner agreement with clause checklist completed
- Finance: sample settlement file validated, GL mappings provided, chart of accounts entries verified
- Partner Ops: SFTP/S3 endpoint, sample file delivery, test ingestion complete
- SRE: evidence of provisioning and usage logs accessible to Finance for audit

Governance and Exceptions

- Any deviation from this playbook (e.g., off-cycle settlements, non-standard commission terms) requires a written exception approved by Finance VP and Legal Counsel. Exceptions must be recorded in the Contract Exceptions registry and reviewed quarterly.

Frequently Asked Questions (short)

Q: When do we treat partner commissions as prepaid vs accrual?
A: Commissions are accrued when the related revenue is earned. If partner is paid in advance, record as Partner Prepaid and amortize against commission expense as the related revenue is recognized.

Q: How should taxes be handled for cross-border partner billings?
A: Tax treatment depends on merchant-of-record and local VAT/sales tax rules. Finance Tax Owner must approve cross-border tax treatment prior to first settlement.
